label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A long pole with a flat blade, used to row a boat.
ex: She pulled hard on the oar to reach the shore.
note: The tool used for rowing, as a paddle is for a canoe.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Something you must do because of a law, promise, or duty.
ex: Parents have a legal obligation to send their children to school.
note: Related forms: oblige, obligatory; contrast with an option or choice.

label: READING
def: Forced or required to do something by law, duty, or circumstances.
ex: After the scandal, the minister felt obliged to resign.
note: Also means grateful: "I'm much obliged for your help."

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A building with telescopes for watching the stars and planets.
ex: Astronomers at the observatory tracked the comet for weeks.
note: Place and activity: an observatory is where observation happens.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Having no smell at all.
ex: Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it is odorless and invisible.
note: From odor (a smell); compare tasteless and colorless.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Out of tune; not matching the correct musical notes.
ex: His off-key singing made the whole audience wince.
note: Also figurative: an off-key remark is unsuitable for the situation.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: An illegal act or a crime; also, a feeling of being insulted.
ex: Driving without a license is a serious offense.
note: To take offense means to feel hurt or insulted; in sport, the attacking side.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To leave out or fail to include something.
ex: The editor omitted two paragraphs to shorten the article.
note: Noun: omission; an omission can be deliberate or accidental.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Willing to consider new ideas and opinions without prejudice.
ex: An open-minded judge listens carefully to both sides.
note: Contrast with narrow-minded or dogmatic.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A piece of land where fruit trees are grown.
ex: We picked apples in the orchard behind the farmhouse.
note: Pairs in analogies: orchard is to fruit trees as vineyard is to grapes.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A scientist who studies birds.
ex: The ornithologist recorded the migration routes of the storks.
note: Specialist and subject: ornithologist to birds, as entomologist to insects.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The final result of an action, process, or event.
ex: Nobody could predict the outcome of the close election.
note: Outcome is the result; the cause or input comes before it.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: No longer current, modern, or useful.
ex: The factory still relies on outdated machinery from the 1970s.
note: Close to obsolete, which is stronger: no longer used at all.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To describe the main points of something without full detail.
ex: The manager outlined the new plan in a short meeting.
note: As a noun, an outline is a summary or the edge shape of an object.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To remove a ruler or government from power by force.
ex: The rebels tried to overthrow the military regime.
note: Stronger than criticize or oppose: it means actually removing from power.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A flat shellfish that lives in the sea and can produce pearls.
ex: A single oyster may take years to form a pearl.
note: Producer and product: oyster to pearl, as bee to honey.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A small group of people chosen to discuss, judge, or advise.
ex: A panel of experts reviewed the research proposals.
note: Also a flat piece of material, as in a solar panel.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Loss of the ability to move part or all of the body.
ex: The accident caused temporary paralysis in his left arm.
note: Figuratively, a complete inability to act: political paralysis.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An organism that lives on or in another and feeds on it.
ex: The tick is a parasite that feeds on the blood of animals.
note: Figuratively, a person who lives off others without giving back.

label: READING
def: To analyze a sentence by breaking it into its grammatical parts.
ex: The students parsed each sentence to find the subject and verb.
note: More broadly, to examine something closely in order to understand it.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An activity done regularly for enjoyment in one's free time.
ex: Reading detective novels is her favorite pastime.
note: A pastime is chosen for pleasure, unlike a job or duty.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who gives money or support to an artist or cause.
ex: The wealthy patron paid for the young painter's studies.
note: Also a regular customer of a shop or restaurant.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make it easier for something to happen later.
ex: Early experiments paved the way for modern vaccines.
note: Similar to lay the groundwork; the result comes afterward.

label: READING
def: Strange or unusual, often in a slightly disturbing way.
ex: There was a peculiar smell coming from the basement.
note: Peculiar to means belonging only to: a custom peculiar to the region.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Likely to spoil or decay quickly, especially food.
ex: Milk and fish are perishable, so keep them refrigerated.
note: Opposite: durable or long-lasting; related verb: perish.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Allowed by rules or law.
ex: Using a calculator is not permissible during this test.
note: Close to permitted; opposite: forbidden or prohibited.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To continue to exist or to keep doing something despite difficulty.
ex: If the pain persists, you should see a doctor.
note: Adjective: persistent; noun: persistence.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: One of the colored, leaf-like parts of a flower.
ex: The rose lost its petals after a week in the vase.
note: Part and whole: petal to flower, as page to book.

label: READING
def: A scholar who studies languages and texts, especially their history.
ex: The philologist traced the word back to ancient Greek.
note: Specialist and field: philologist to language, as historian to the past.

label: READING
def: Relating to the sounds of human speech.
ex: The dictionary gives a phonetic spelling to show pronunciation.
note: Noun: phonetics, the study of speech sounds.

label: READING
def: A starting point for a journey, discussion, or line of thought.
ex: The author uses a childhood memory as a point of departure.
note: Also the literal place a journey begins.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A survey of people's opinions, or the process of voting.
ex: A recent poll shows most citizens support the new law.
note: The polls also means the place of voting: a polling station.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who makes pots and dishes from clay.
ex: The potter shaped the wet clay on a spinning wheel.
note: Maker and product: potter to pottery, as weaver to cloth.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Rain, snow, or hail that falls to the ground.
ex: The region receives very little precipitation in summer.
note: In chemistry, the forming of a solid from a liquid.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An animal that hunts and eats other animals.
ex: The lion is the main predator on the savanna.
note: Opposite role: prey; adjective: predatory.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Decided or fixed in advance.
ex: Each player moves according to a predetermined set of rules.
note: Contrast with spontaneous or chosen on the spot.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Something that must exist or happen before something else can.
ex: A basic course in statistics is a prerequisite for this class.
note: Close to precondition; do not confuse with perquisite (a perk).

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To suppose something is true without full proof.
ex: I presume the meeting is canceled, since nobody has arrived.
note: Also to act too boldly; adjective: presumptuous.

label: READING
def: To assume something in advance as a basis for an argument.
ex: The plan presupposes that the budget will not be cut.
note: Noun: presupposition; similar to take for granted.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A false reason given to hide the real reason for an action.
ex: He visited on the pretext of borrowing a book.
note: A pretext is an excuse, not the true motive.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To make a small hole in something with a sharp point.
ex: She pricked her finger on a thorn in the garden.
note: A needle or thorn pricks; the result is a tiny puncture.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Existing or happening before something else.
ex: No prior experience is needed for this job.
note: Prior to means before; noun: priority.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A special right or advantage given only to certain people.
ex: Having a private tutor was a privilege few students enjoyed.
note: Adjective: privileged; contrast with a right shared by everyone.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Very great or intense; also, showing deep understanding.
ex: The discovery had a profound effect on modern medicine.
note: Opposite: superficial or shallow.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An official rule forbidding something.
ex: The city introduced a prohibition on smoking in parks.
note: Verb: prohibit; opposite: permission.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To increase rapidly in number or spread widely.
ex: Online news sites have proliferated over the past decade.
note: Noun: proliferation; stronger than simply grow.

label: READING
def: Continuing for a long time, often longer than expected.
ex: Prolonged exposure to the sun can damage the skin.
note: Verb: prolong, to make something last longer.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To help something grow or succeed; also, to raise someone's job rank.
ex: Regular exercise and a balanced diet promote good health.
note: Noun: promotion, which can also mean advertising a product.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Biased information spread to influence public opinion.
ex: The regime used radio propaganda to glorify its leader.
note: Propaganda aims to persuade, not to inform fairly.

label: READING
def: To spread ideas or beliefs widely; also, to breed plants.
ex: The group propagated its views through leaflets and speeches.
note: Noun: propagation; related to propaganda.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The legal process of charging someone with a crime in court.
ex: The prosecution presented evidence against the accused.
note: The opposing side in a trial is the defense.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Supplies of food and other necessities, especially for a journey.
ex: The explorers carried provisions for three months.
note: In the singular, a provision is also a condition in a law or contract.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To postpone something to a later time.
ex: They put off the meeting until next week.
note: Also to discourage: the smell put me off the food.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To trust or believe in someone or something completely.
ex: Many voters put their faith in the young candidate.
note: Similar to rely on; the trust may later prove mistaken.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Difficult to understand or explain.
ex: The results of the experiment were puzzling to everyone.
note: Similar to baffling or perplexing.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Having the skills or training needed for a job or task.
ex: Only a qualified electrician should repair the wiring.
note: A qualified statement is limited or partial, not complete.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A field of activity or interest; also, a kingdom.
ex: The question lies outside the realm of science.
note: Within the realm of possibility means possible.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who fights against or refuses to obey authority.
ex: The rebels seized control of the northern province.
note: As a verb (to reBEL), to resist authority; noun: rebellion.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Given or felt by each side toward the other; mutual.
ex: The two countries signed a reciprocal trade agreement.
note: In math, the reciprocal of a number is 1 divided by it.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A vote by all citizens on a single political question.
ex: The government held a referendum on the new constitution.
note: Unlike an election, which chooses people, a referendum decides an issue.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To stop yourself from doing something.
ex: Please refrain from talking during the performance.
note: Usually followed by from; as a noun, the repeated chorus of a song.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A government, especially one that rules strictly or unfairly.
ex: The regime banned all opposition newspapers.
note: Also a system of rules or a plan: a diet regime.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A large permanent unit of soldiers in an army.
ex: His grandfather served in a cavalry regiment.
note: Part and whole: soldier to regiment, as player to team.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To control something by rules or to keep it at a steady level.
ex: The body regulates its temperature by sweating.
note: Noun: regulation, an official rule.

label: READING
def: To explain or understand something in a new or different way.
ex: The film reinterprets a classic story for modern audiences.
note: Noun: reinterpretation; implies an earlier interpretation existed.

label: READING
def: The raised or hollowed shape of a surface; also, a feeling of ease.
ex: The map shows the mountain's relief in shades of brown.
note: More common meaning: the ease felt when worry or pain ends.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A small part that remains after the rest is gone.
ex: Only remnants of the ancient wall still stand.
note: Close to residue and remains; the whole no longer exists.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To formally give up a right, claim, or belief.
ex: He renounced his citizenship and moved abroad.
note: Noun: renunciation; stronger and more formal than stop.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An exact copy of an object, often smaller.
ex: The museum displays a replica of the ancient ship.
note: A replica copies an original; it is not a fake meant to deceive.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The use of force to control people and limit their freedom.
ex: Years of repression led to mass protests.
note: In psychology, pushing painful memories out of awareness.

label: READING
def: What remains after the main part has gone or been removed.
ex: A sticky residue was left where the label had been.
note: Similar to remnant; plural: residues.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Not easily harmed or affected by something; opposing change.
ex: This fabric is resistant to water and stains.
note: Noun: resistance; heat-resistant, drug-resistant.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A rule or limit on what people can do.
ex: The city placed restrictions on water use during the drought.
note: Verb: restrict; opposite: freedom or permission.

label: READING
def: To keep or continue to have something.
ex: The old building retains much of its original charm.
note: Noun: retention; opposite: lose or release.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Money that a business or government receives, especially from sales.
ex: The company's revenue doubled after the product launch.
note: Revenue is income before costs; profit is what remains after costs.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A return to strength, popularity, or use after a decline.
ex: The 1990s saw a revival of interest in vinyl records.
note: Verb: revive; contrast with decline.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To move in a circle around a central point.
ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun once a year.
note: Figuratively, to revolve around means to center on: the plot revolves around a theft.

label: READING
def: Strict and unwilling to change; also, stiff and not bendable.
ex: The school had rigid rules about uniforms.
note: Opposite: flexible.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person or group competing with another for the same goal.
ex: The two companies have been rivals for decades.
note: Noun: rivalry, the state of competing.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person whose behavior others admire and copy.
ex: The coach is a role model for many young athletes.
note: Being a role model is about example, not formal authority.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To officially introduce a new product, service, or plan.
ex: The company will roll out the new app next month.
note: Noun: rollout; often gradual, region by region.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A story passed among people that may not be true.
ex: A rumor spread that the factory would close.
note: Rumors are unconfirmed; contrast with verified facts.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: One of the horizontal bars that form the steps of a ladder.
ex: He climbed carefully, testing each rung of the ladder.
note: Part and whole: rung to ladder, as step to staircase.
